blurb: Cheese and dairy jokes, aged to perfection. Wisconsin fans welcome.

questions.q: What do you call cheese that isn't yours?
questions.fact: Bonus: What do you call a cheese that's feeling sad? Blue cheese.

questions.q: What did the cheese say when it looked in the mirror?
questions.fact: Bonus: How do you make a milkshake? Give it a good scare.

questions.q: What kind of cheese would you use to disguise a small horse?
questions.fact: Bonus: What cheese do you use to coax a bear out of its cave? Camembert. (Come on, bear!)
questions.src: classic; mascarpone sounds like 'mask a pony'

questions.q: What cheese is made backward?
questions.fact: The pun: Edam spelled backward is 'made.' The cheese is named after the town of Edam in the Netherlands.
questions.src: classic; premise: Edam cheese is named for the town of Edam, North Holland

questions.q: Who's the boss of the refrigerator?
questions.fact: Bonus: What kind of cheese guards a castle? Moatzarella.
questions.src: classic; 'the big cheese' is an old idiom for the person in charge

questions.q: I quit my job at the cheese shop. The work was just too ___
questions.fact: Bonus: How should you handle a dangerous cheese? Caerphilly. (Caerphilly is a real cheese from Wales.)
questions.src: original; grating = annoying and shredding cheese. Bonus classic; premise: Caerphilly is a Welsh cheese

questions.q: The cheese shelf at the deli collapsed. All that was left was ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the yogurt go to the art museum? It was cultured.
questions.src: classic (adapted from the cheese-factory version, no explosion); de-brie = debris

questions.q: What did the cheese say when it showed up late to the party?
questions.fact: Bonus: What did the cheese say to the photographer? Say people!
questions.src: classic; feta late = better late. Distractors are cheese puns on leaving phrases, not on being late

questions.q: I'm very strict about cheese. I only eat it on days that end in ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the cheese turn down the deal? It had grater plans.
questions.src: classic one-liner pattern (every day of the week ends in Y)

questions.q: The waiter began grating parmesan and said, 'Just say when.' I'm very shy, so ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the cheddar win the argument? All of its points were sharp.

questions.q: I have a great cheese joke, but it isn't ready yet. It still needs to ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Did you hear about the Wisconsin cheese that saved the day? It was legen-dairy.
questions.src: classic idea (cheese joke that needs to age), wording original

questions.q: The deli sells Swiss cheese by the pound. So, technically, the holes are ___
questions.fact: The pun: you pay by weight and air weighs next to nothing, so the holes cost you nothing. Bacteria make the gas that forms them.
questions.src: original; premise: Swiss cheese eyes form from carbon dioxide made by propionic bacteria (Propionibacterium freudenreichii)

questions.q: Why did the kitten volunteer in the school nurse's office?

questions.q: Why are dogs such bad dancers?

questions.q: My dog is so smart. I asked him what two minus two is, and he said ___

questions.q: What did one wall say to the other wall?

questions.q: Why was the broom late?

questions.q: Why did the teacher wear sunglasses to class?

We match, let's take a photo

Hang around, I'll go on ahead

questions.q: Why do you go to bed at night?
options: The bed won't come to you

questions.q: Did you hear the joke about the roof? Never mind, ___

questions.q: What's the number one cause of dry skin?

blurb: Tools, building and handyman jokes, measured twice and told once

questions.q: Why did the hammer ace its big test?
questions.fact: Bonus: Which tool is best at math? Multi-pliers.

questions.q: What did the paint say to the wall?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why are electricians always up to date? They follow current events.

questions.q: What did the drill ask the hammer?
questions.fact: Bonus: What did the doorknob say to the door? Let's get a handle on this.

questions.q: What's the best way to carve wood?
questions.fact: The pun: 'whittle by whittle' sounds like 'little by little,' and to whittle is to carve wood a shaving at a time.
questions.src: classic; premise: whittling is carving wood by shaving off small pieces

questions.q: Want to hear a joke about construction?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the ladder get promoted? It kept stepping up.
questions.src: classic (bonus swapped: the Velcro line is credited to a comedian)

questions.q: Why did the saw go to the party?
questions.fact: Bonus: I'm afraid of elevators, so I'm taking steps to avoid them.
questions.src: classic; cut loose = have fun, and saws cut (replaced the glue-book joke in check)

questions.q: The woodworker's son is just like his dad. He's ___
options: a chip off the old block
questions.fact: The pun: 'a chip off the old block' means a kid just like a parent, and woodworkers chip pieces off blocks of wood.
questions.src: original on the old idiom (replaced the carpenter's-level joke in check)

questions.q: My carpenter friend can never make up his mind. He's always ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Why is the new fence so popular online? It has great posts.
questions.src: original; distractors are carpentry idioms that don't mean undecided

questions.q: My 'self-assembly' bookshelf arrived three weeks ago, and it still hasn't ___
questions.fact: Bonus: What did the wall say to the shelf? Hang in there.

questions.q: At the hardware store I asked for nails. The clerk said, 'How long do you want them?' I said ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the tape measure get the job? It really measured up.

questions.q: I bought a do-it-yourself guide to fixing pipes. Page one says ___
questions.fact: Bonus: What kind of shoes do plumbers wear? Clogs.

questions.q: I've cut this board three times, and it's still ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Why does the handyman always carry a pencil? He has to draw the line somewhere.
questions.src: classic carpenter's joke (cutting only makes a board shorter); replaced the building/built line in check

blurb: The cleverest one-liners and sneakiest twists. Think twice, then pick.

questions.q: Why did the shoe salesman lose his job?
questions.fact: Bonus: What kind of shoes does a lazy person wear? Loafers.
questions.src: classic; the boot = fired (replaced the banker joke and the three-lefts bonus in check)

questions.q: Why did the person keep their money in the freezer?
questions.fact: Bonus: I'm great at keeping secrets. It's the people I tell them to who aren't.

questions.q: What's the difference between ignorance and apathy?
options: One is worse than the other
I don't know and I don't care
questions.fact: Bonus: My friend said apathy is a big problem. I told him, 'Whatever.'
questions.src: classic; the answer shows both: not knowing (ignorance) and not caring (apathy)

questions.q: What do you call a magician who has lost their magic?
questions.fact: The pun: take the word 'magic' out of 'magician' and all that's left is 'ian.'

questions.q: I tried to start a hide-and-seek contest, but ___
options: good players are hard to find
questions.fact: Bonus: Have you met my friend, the hide-and-seek champion? Me neither.

questions.q: I spent all afternoon staring into the mirror. I guess I needed some ___
questions.fact: Bonus: I couldn't remember how to throw a boomerang. Then it came back to me.
questions.src: original; reflection = deep thought and a mirror image (replaced the mood-ring line in check)

questions.q: I have a photographic memory, but it never ___
questions.fact: The pun: camera film had to be developed before anyone could see the pictures, so this memory never came out.
questions.src: classic; premise: photographic film must be chemically developed to show an image

questions.q: I held the door open for a clown. I thought it was a nice ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the clown go to the doctor? He was feeling a little funny.

questions.q: I'm so good at sleeping, I can do it ___
questions.fact: Bonus: I'm not one to brag, but I'm the most humble person I know.

questions.q: I used to be indecisive. Now ___
questions.fact: Bonus: I started a club for people who can't make decisions. We're still picking a name.

questions.q: People keep telling me I'm condescending. ___
options: It means I talk down to people
I'm working hard to fix that
I really don't see it myself

questions.q: The psychic convention was canceled this year due to ___
